title: Representing Collections and Empty Values
learning_outcomes: Explain how representing collections and empty values affects an API contract or implementation.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on representing collections and empty values in json and data representations. You will connect empty arrays and empty objects to a concrete API contract decision, inspect a small example, and decide what evidence proves the behavior is correct.
content.why_it_matters: Representing Collections and Empty Values matters because API consumers depend on predictable behavior even when clients, servers, networks, and stored data evolve independently. Applying empty arrays and empty objects deliberately reduces ambiguity, makes failures easier to diagnose, and gives tests a clear expectation.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: JSON is a representation format; decide types, nullability, field exposure, and compatibility as part of the public schema. In this lesson, treat “Representing Collections and Empty Values” as a design or implementation decision: name the expected behavior, identify its boundary, and verify it with a representative request or test.

content_blocks.title: Inspect the pattern: Representing Collections and Empty Values
content_blocks.expected_output: The JSON object has stable public fields, typed values, an explicit nullable date, and a collection of tags.

content_blocks.title: Walkthrough
content_blocks.text: Start with “Empty arrays and empty objects”; it establishes the vocabulary for this topic. Next, compare it with “Null versus missing properties” and “Backward compatibility of response fields”. In a real API, write down the observable behavior first, then test one normal request and one invalid or unauthorized request. Keep resource state, caller identity, and internal implementation details separate.

content_blocks.title: Professional review check
content_blocks.text: Treat a response body as a public contract; never leak internal persistence fields by default. The worked snippet is intentionally inspectable, not an executable hosted API. Replace example.test and placeholder identifiers with local test data only when you implement the lesson project.

Separate a transport failure from an application validation failure, authorization denial, and dependency/database failure.

common_mistakes: Treating representing collections and empty values as an implementation detail rather than a documented behavior.
Testing only the happy path and ignoring malformed, unauthorized, conflicting, duplicate, or dependency-failure cases.
Publishing an example without checking version assumptions, sensitive-data exposure, and the expected output.
